summary: Admit Russian Post one-page easy-return PDF labels through the existing bounded label reader.

impacts.evidence: The existing tenant-scoped logistics account and permission path remains the source of the label request.
The PDF is handled as bounded binary data and only an opaque digest reference leaves host transport.
The existing provider-neutral LabelRequest and LabelResult contracts are reused.
No event envelope, event type or event payload changes.
The existing logistics.label.read capability and SDK interface remain unchanged.
No database columns, mappings or durable provider payloads are added.
The RPO and provider PDF response are bounded before egress and artifact publication.
The existing label permission and outbound policy continue to gate the read operation.
Existing label operation lineage records the opaque artifact reference without PDF contents.
A label read is repeatable, while timeout and malformed responses cannot yield a fabricated artifact.
The transport adds one fixed-host HTTPS GET under the existing host-mediated egress boundary.
The existing logistics timeout, rate and error normalization policy covers the additional GET.
Removing the existing label capability or provider support entry disables new return-label reads without migration.
Deterministic tests verify the exact easy-return path, auth headers, PDF validation and invalid-RPO rejection.
